$comment: Known-open findings from rendered-resource-requests.ts, each with a reason and a lift
condition. An entry that matches nothing is STALE and fails the audit -- an acknowledgement
that outlives its defect is how a baseline becomes a lie.
Every liftsWhen here is the GATE ITSELF rather than a paraphrase of it. A lift condition
stricter than its gate keeps an entry alive after the defect is gone, which has cost this

entries.reason: THE `infra/k8s/applications` TREE IS A SECOND APP-OF-APPS ROOT THAT NO RUNG COVERS. infra/k8s/applications/root-application.yaml is `zeta-root`, auto-applied by K3S via services.k3s.manifests on first boot, so on a metal node it is applied alongside the full-ai-cluster tree. The CPU/memory ladder in storage-profiles.json keys its rows by a directory relative to full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications and has no way to name a row in another tree, so every rung total -- including the `metal` substrate cell, which sums 47 Applications for 9256m -- excludes this tree entirely. MEASURED 2026-08-22 by rendering all seven at both rungs: 4035m / 8837Mi, of which infra/gitlab is 2525m and infra/cockroachdb is 1500m. Adding that to the metal cohort gives 13291m, which still fits the 57000m cluster-sum budget, so no conclusion in this PR turns on it -- but a total that silently omits a whole root is the exact shape of understatement this checker exists to refuse, and it is recorded rather than rounded off. Closing it needs a tree-qualified key in the catalogue (`<tree>/<dir>`), which is a schema change to a file three other checkers read and is deliberately not bundled with a bring-up-facing change. This entry: infra/argorollouts renders 0m at rung "dev".
